tasks.title: Durable job queue (lease/heartbeat/reclaim, window-aware, priority, cap)

prep.what: Build the durable, crash-safe job queue that the sweeper and CI/deploy system will run on — the backbone that serializes and distributes all agent work.
prep.understand: The Phase 6 sweeper (t21) needs a durable job queue. 'Durable' means a job survives process crashes: the lease/heartbeat pattern ensures a dead consumer's job is reclaimed and retried. 'Window-aware' means jobs only fire during the configured work window. Priority and cap bound in-flight concurrency. This is the first and most load-bearing piece of Phase 6 — the sweeper, CI lane, and deploy system all queue through it.
approach: Design the `jobs` table schema: `id`, `queue_name`, `payload json`, `status` (queued/leased/done/failed), `priority int`, `lease_token uuid nullable`, `leased_at timestamptz`, `heartbeat_at timestamptz`, `reclaim_after_s int`, `window_start time`, `window_end time`, `enqueued_at`, `created_at`.

Implement `claim(queue, worker_id)` atomically with a single `UPDATE ... WHERE status='queued' AND lease_token IS NULL ORDER BY priority DESC, enqueued_at ASC LIMIT 1 RETURNING *` — Postgres handles the race without application-level locking.
Implement `heartbeat(job_id, lease_token)` (periodic UPDATE on `heartbeat_at`) and a `reclaimer` function that marks stale leased jobs back to `queued` where `now() - heartbeat_at > reclaim_after_s`.
Add window-aware dispatch: a helper that checks `now() BETWEEN window_start AND window_end` before a worker calls claim — gates the whole fleet off-hours with a single predicate.
Write the tests: concurrent claim doesn't double-issue the same job; crash-reclaim fires after heartbeat goes stale; window blocks dispatch outside hours; priority ordering is respected.
resources: claude-todos-skill: `db/migrate.ts` (the PG migration runner — add a new numbered migration for the `jobs` table)
